concept.title: Applicability attributes
concept.shortdesc: Standard DITA filtering attributes on any map entry, topic or element decide which readers see it. One rule covers both the reader's release and what their organization is entitled to.

section.title: The attributes

sthead.stentry: A reader sees the content when

strow.stentry: their organization holds at least one listed product
their organization holds at least one listed feature
their version matches at least one listed range
the build-time DITAVAL does not exclude them

section.p: For example, this site declares product: [core, hosted, embed]. The self-hosting guides carry product="core", the embedded-help section carries product="embed", and the architecture overview carries product="core hosted" because it matters to anyone with either.

section.title: How conditions combine

ul.li: Values within one attribute are alternatives: product="core hosted" shows to a reader holding either.
Separate attributes must all pass: product="embed" release="0.2.." needs the embed product and release 0.2 or later.
A condition on an ancestor applies to everything inside it: an element, a topic, a topicref or a topichead.
A topic is published to a reader only when a navigation entry they can see points at it and the topic's own root passes.

section.title: Reader attributes and build attributes
section.p: product, feature and release are reader attributes: they are kept in the release snapshot and decided for each reader at request time. The other attributes are build attributes: the build-time DITAVAL decides them once for everyone, and readers are never gated by them. So audience="admin" labels content, but does not hide it from anyone unless the DITAVAL excludes that value. Use product or feature to gate readers.

ul.li: Content their filter excludes, in pages, navigation, search, the help panel or PDFs.
The title of a hidden topic: a link to it renders as its authored text only. See .
Filtering attributes themselves: they are stripped from the HTML.
